key_insight: EvoDuet co-evolves web search queries and candidate solutions so an LLM can fetch better evidence exactly when its knowledge is insufficient, improving scientific-discovery search quality without changing model parameters.
engineering_relevance: The method adds a retrieval gate plus inner/outer evolutionary loops to make LLM-based optimization more robust in knowledge-heavy tasks where naive web search repeatedly returns stale or unhelpful pages.
method: Retrieval gate lets the LLM decide whether to search, reuse stored documents, or solve without retrieval.
Inner loop refines search queries and ranks documents by the solution quality they are expected to produce.
Outer loop generates candidate solutions in parallel from retrieved documents and logs outcomes for future searches.
evidence_signal: Across 21 optimization tasks, EvoDuet improved OpenEvolve normalized discovery gain from 74.1% to 78.0% with GPT-5.6-Luna and from 61.3% to 82.3% with Gemini-3.8-Flash, with best runs surpassing prior scores on eight tasks.
watch_item: Benefits are model- and scaffold-dependent, since Qwen3.5-9B did not improve and the method still relies on effective retrieval/document ranking in each iteration.
paper_title: EvoDuet: Bilevel Co-Evolution of Web Searching and Task Solving for Scientific Discovery
